name: BattleScene_SpawnMonstersByProgress
summary: Event-battle monster spawner: reads two game-work flags (+0x27508/+0x275A4) and a per-unit byte, then picks up to two monster ids (0x342..0x345, 0x391, 0xC9, 199, 200) with counts 1-3 from a progress float (thresholds 20/30/40/50/60/70), finds a battle group slot for each and spawns that many units.
evidence: Named callees settle it: BattleScene_SpawnMonsterUnit(battleScene, groupSlot, monsterId, 0, 0) is called in a loop and the group slot comes from Menu_FindSlotForEntry, which is the same 0x0020B100 per-column predicate BattleScene_SpawnMonsterUnit uses for its four unit groups (+0x4254/+0x4270/+0x428C/+0x4298). No item code at all: the old 'Item_GrantRewardItems' read the 0x342-family ids as item ids, but they are monster ids handed to the spawner.

name: Field_NpcRef_GetTalkAttrByte

params.npcRef: NPC reference record; u16 at +4 is the field-NPC entry id

summary: Returns the talk/speaker attribute byte for an NPC reference (0xFF when the reference is empty). Looks the entry up in the active field scene NPC table and, when its own byte is 0xFF, falls back through the entry's u16 +0x0E into the data-manager table.
evidence: The three callers are now named Squirrel-bound message natives - FukidashiMessage (speech bubble), InnMessage and MessageFunc - and all three use the result to choose how the NPC speaks, which is exactly the 'talk attribute' reading. The fallback chain (entry->u16_0E -> 0x0063E2BC -> dataMgr->f_3E4->f_10 + idx*8 + 4) is a second table of the same byte, not an icon id.

name: maybe_BattleAi_PickRandomTargetAboveDamage
signature: void* maybe_BattleAi_PickRandomTargetAboveDamage(void* aiCtx, u32 skillId, void* preferredTarget)

params.aiCtx: battle AI context (16 target-unit buckets of 0x9BC bytes at +0x10)
params.preferredTarget: target tried first when no bucket qualifies

summary: Target picker for the battle AI: walks the 16 target-unit buckets, keeps those that are alive and accept the given skill (vtable +0x18/+0xF8/+0xFC), estimates damage with Battle_ApplyDamageClamp and returns one of the units whose damage exceeds the record threshold at +0x147, chosen with the battle RNG. Falls back to the preferred target.
evidence: The caller BattleAi_FilterUsableCandidates assigns the result to a single candidate pointer (k = ...) and reads k->f_e2, so it returns one chosen unit, not a filtered list - the old 'FilterOffensiveCandidates' name described an in-place filter that does not exist. The 0x9BC stride matches the documented 16 target-unit buckets, and the final func_001CA474(rng+0x4218, 0, count-1) is a random pick. Kept below 0.5 because Ghidra leaves local_e4 as a null pointer that is then dereferenced (local_e4->f_e2), so the skill-id plumbing is damaged.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_InitFromTriggerRecord

params.self: field gadget; f_2EC is the trigger id, f_2C8..f_2E0 receive the record fields

summary: Gadget vtable slot 1: when the field-trigger bit for f_2EC is not set it fills the gadget's four u16 slots with 0xFFFF defaults; otherwise it copies the four u16 fields of the 8-byte field-trigger record into f_2C8/f_2D0/f_2DC/f_2E0 and queues gadget command 7.
evidence: The record comes from 0x0063DCE8, the field-trigger table (8-byte rows in dm->f_8FC, ids < 0x306), and the gate is 0x0066B3B0, the trigger-bitmask test on (work+0x24A98)+0x5418 - so the four u16s are trigger-record fields, not animation slots as the old name claimed. What the gadget then does with them is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Casino_Poker_SwapTenSlots
summary: Poker deal variant: reshuffles the rank order (Casino_Poker_ShuffleDeck13) and the suit order (Casino_Poker_ShuffleDeck4), then for ten (rank,suit) pairs looks the deck entry up with func_00416638 and swaps it into the hand slots two bytes at a time.
evidence: The three named neighbours (Casino_Poker_ShuffleDeck13, Casino_Poker_ShuffleDeck4, Casino_Poker_ShuffleU16) confirm the poker-deck reading, but nothing in the new context says which deal variant this is or why it swaps ten pairs, so the specific 'SwapTenSlots' wording stays a hypothesis.

name: Field_InteractJob_Begin

params.self: interaction job; f_45 receives the state, f_46 the record byte

summary: Start method of the field interaction job: inspects the current interaction target, sets state 0 for the 'x' kind, otherwise resolves its record and sets state 2 when the player can see the point and 1 when not, then raises event trigger command 0x10 or 0x11.
evidence: Both callees are now named and match the summary one for one: Field_IsPointVisible decides state 2 vs 1 and Event_OnTriggerCommand(work+0x6C, 0x10/0x11) raises the trigger. The three Os_GetGameWork reads are the documented (work+8)->+0x88 Field2D manager and +0x54 object manager.

name: maybe_BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelAttachmentsB
signature: int maybe_BattleScene_UpdateUnitModelAttachmentsB(Battle2DScene* self, int side, unsigned* additional, int additional2)
summary: Second (Thumb) decode of the unit-model attachment update: walks one side's unit list, resolves each unit's model record and compares the model's position against the unit's, breaking out when the sign of the difference changes.

name: Battle_IsUnitModelVisible
signature: bool Battle_IsUnitModelVisible(void* work, void* obj, unsigned short modelId)

params.obj: scene object; f_768 is the body id

summary: Decides whether a unit's model is shown in the current battle presentation: the model record's +0x3E flag must be set, body id 400 always passes, and a short whitelist (0x13D, 0x13E, 0x13F, 0x28A, 0x358, 0x3A5, 0x3B9) passes only while the battle 3D-mode byte +0x4244 is set.
evidence: The named callers are Actor_NotifyComponentEvent, Actor_ResetComponents, Actor_SetComponentFlag and Model_SetupFromTypeId, i.e. actor component/model setup, and the two inputs are a model id (resolved through 0x0063E05C to a record whose +0x3E flag gates it) and the object's body id - so the predicate is about the model, not about a battle unit. Renamed from IsUnitVisibleInBattle, which said 'unit' twice and hid the model/body-id keying.

name: BattleScene_PreloadUnitModelVariants
signature: void BattleScene_PreloadUnitModelVariants(BattleScene* self, void** entries, int count)

params.entries: array of scene objects; +0x10 is a skip flag, +0x768 the body id

The entries are scene objects, not party members, so 'MemberModelVariants' was too narrow; std_ConstructArray is the usual mis-marked noreturn CRT helper.

name: maybe_BattleAi_FindTargetMatchingMetric
signature: void* maybe_BattleAi_FindTargetMatchingMetric(void* aiCtx, u32 request, int mode)

params.aiCtx: battle AI context; +0x9BD0 is the 16-entry target-unit pointer array
params.request: data-manager record id supplying the target metric

summary: Battle-AI target selection: walks the 16 target units at aiCtx+0x9BD0, computes each one's size ratio from its vtable +0x90/+0x94 values, compares it with the metric taken from the record for `request` (three float fields, picked by `mode` and the battle 3D-mode byte +0x4247) and returns the unit that fits best.
evidence: The caller is BattleAi_EvaluateSpellAndSkillScores, which passes its own aiCtx as the first argument, and aiCtx+0x9BD0..+0x9C10 is exactly 16 pointers - the 16 target-unit buckets that end where the 0x7C x 0x14 candidate array at +0x9C10 begins. So this is AI target selection, not UI text layout; the old name came from the poisoned Ui_TextLayout_* range. Kept below 0.5 because the exact metric (which of the three floats) is still unclear.

name: maybe_Battle_RollUnitVisibilityChance

params.self: action model; f_768 is the body id used for the record lookup

summary: Probability gate used when syncing battle unit models: for kinds 2/8/10/11/12/0x90 it succeeds outright when the model record's +0x108 flag is set, otherwise it rolls the battle RNG against 25%; kinds 3/9 roll against 12.5% or 67.5% depending on the same flag. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: The caller Battle_ActionModel_UpdateUnitVisibility uses the result to decide whether to call the action model's vtable +0x128 for a unit id, and the record it reads is the per-model one from 0x0063E5C8 (byte +0x108), so this is a unit-visibility roll, not an 'action chance'. The kind switch itself is still unexplained, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ModePane_UpdateVisibility

params.self: UI widget; +0xB2 is the mode byte
params.reason: 0 forces a full refresh of the three flags

summary: Event handler that shows exactly one of the three game-work flags 0x1A7/0x1A8/0x1A9 (at (work+0x24A98)+0x2A70) according to the widget's mode byte +0xB2, clears the other two, then walks the sibling widgets of class 0x007C4BA8 and refreshes them.

Nothing says the widget is a 'mode pane' specifically, so the name stays a hypothesis.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyRenderPriority

params.self: field scene object; f_B4/f_B0 select the 2D actor, f_B8->f_128 receives the priority byte

summary: Resolves the object's 2D actor through the Field2D manager (work+8->+0x88, helpers 0x0062C388/0x0062C3B0 on f_B4/f_B0) and, when it exists, stores the actor's sprite-priority byte into the object's render child at +0x128.

name: maybe_Field2D_ApplyActorVisualState
signature: void maybe_Field2D_ApplyActorVisualState(void* work, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_CanShowMarkers

params.self: UI overlay; +0x283 is the enable flag, +0x27C selects player vs camera target, +0x281 the mode

summary: Returns 1 when the overlay may draw its markers: flag +0x283 must be set, the referenced object must be idle (+0x44/+0x45 clear) and, depending on +0x27C, either the player actor or the camera-target actor must be in an allowed state (1/2/9 or 1/2/4/5) with a resolvable model; the global block flag work+0x27721 forces 0.

name: Battle_GetMaxUnitMetric
signature: float Battle_GetMaxUnitMetric(u32 arg1, int metricKind, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

params.metricKind: 3, 5 or other: which of the three maxima to return

summary: Walks the four battle unit lists (+0x4254/+0x4270/+0x428C/+0x4298, stride 0x1C) and computes three maxima over the active units - a float stat, func_0048F154 and func_0048E2C0 - then returns the one selected by metricKind. Used by the AI to normalise its scores.
evidence: The three callers are now named AI paths (BattleAi_FilterUsableCandidates, Battle_SelectActionForMode, Battle_CanEquipOrUse) and all three use the float to scale candidate scores, which is what a 'max metric over units' is for. The unit walk is the documented 4 x 0x1C battle list layout.

name: Field_Npc_GetDefaultFaceIfUnset
signature: int Field_Npc_GetDefaultFaceIfUnset(const void* npcFace, int checkUiBlock)

params.npcFace: NPC face record; u8 at +6 is the face id, 0xFF meaning unset
params.checkUiBlock: when non-zero, skip while the UI-block byte (work+8)->+0x44 is set

summary: Returns the default face id for an NPC whose own face byte is 0xFF: it checks the UI-block and cutscene bytes, requires an active field scene whose +0x74->+0x1A bit 0x40 is clear, and returns the signed byte +0x14 of the scene record from 0x0066A7D8. Returns 0 when no default applies.
evidence: Both callers are now named face routines - Field_Npc_UpdateFace and Field_Npc_AdvanceFacePattern - and they use the result as the face id to display, which fixes the 'default face when unset' reading. The 0xFF sentinel at npcFace+6 is the same unset marker the face updaters test.

name: Field_NpcEntry_IsFlag0Set

params.entryRef: reference record; u16 at +4 is the field-NPC entry id

summary: Returns 1 when the referenced field-NPC entry exists, has a valid index byte (+9 != 0xFF) and bit 0 of its flags byte (+0xA) is set. Used by the actor natives to test a per-NPC flag.
evidence: The two callers are now named Squirrel-bound actor natives (IsActorQuestRelation, MessageRegistActor) and both use it as a plain yes/no test on the actor's NPC entry, which matches the body. Renamed from EntryRef_* because the entry is resolved through the field-NPC table (work+8->+0xB4 via 0x0066A74C/0x00628EE0), the same table Field_NpcRef_GetTalkAttrByte uses.

name: Ui_Overlay_CheckRowMarker

params.self: overlay row; f_28 is the attached actor handle, f_49 the record id

summary: Decides whether a row's overlay marker is drawn: in overlay mode 0 it reads the row record's flag byte +0x17 and, when the attached actor is not already flagged, projects the actor's position with Camera_SetupProjection; returns the flag when the actor is on screen, otherwise 0.

The record comes from 0x0063D270 and the actor from 0x0022F59C, both consistent with a per-row overlay entry.

name: maybe_Ui_TouchFocus_FlagOverlap
signature: void* maybe_Ui_TouchFocus_FlagOverlap(void** begin, void** end, u32 arg3, void* touchObject)

params.begin: first element of the class-0x7C3330 object list

summary: Touch-focus pass over a list of class-0x7C3330 UI objects: skips objects whose flag word +0x30 does not match, requires both objects to have a resolvable render child, compares their layer byte +0x128 and, in game mode 2, tests whether the touch point falls inside the object's 2D rectangle.

The tail of the function is elided in the decompilation, so what it does on a hit is still unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetScreenClearColor
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetScreenClearColor(int screen, int preset, u32 third)

params.screen: 0 selects the +0x99C render object, anything else +0x964

name: Ui_NpcIcon_UpdateFromRecord

params.rec: icon record; +0x20..+0x2C is the rectangle to centre on

summary: Centres an NPC map icon on the record rectangle (+0x20..+0x2C), applies the world-map highlight and, when the map is idle, registers the icon's four slots once (f_2D8).
evidence: The named sibling Ui_WorldMapMarker_ApplyCurrentHighlight is called from here, and the four maybe_Game_FindRegisteredIndex calls with self->f_288 are the slot registration the summary describes; the record rectangle arithmetic (rec->f_20+f_28, rec->f_24+f_2c, halved by 0.5f) matches 'centre on the record'.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ApplyUnitMessageText
summary: For every unit in the battle party list (+0x4260), resolves the unit's character byte at +0x768 to a party record and, for each of the record's four byte pairs at +0x370, rolls an id in that range with the battle RNG and pushes it to the unit's widget through vtable +0x40; a final value from the record's +0x398 float is pushed the same way.
evidence: The caller is now named (Battle_UpdateUnitCommandPhase) and the party record comes from the documented func_0035EB98, but the pushed ids are RNG-rolled from per-record ranges, which fits random message/voice variation as well as message text - the name keeps the first pass's guess.

name: Field_Gimmick_ReleaseAnchorEffects

params.self: field gimmick; +0x10C/+0x110 are the two effect handles, f_114 the reference count

summary: Releases a gimmick's two anchor effect handles (+0x10C/+0x110) when its f_E4/f_108 phases are clear and both handles are still valid in the 0x007B4D68 handle table, decrements the reference count f_114 and, when it drops below 1, plays animation 2 on the object at +0xC. Always returns 1.

name: maybe_BattleScene_InitAndUpdatePartyStatusFlags
summary: 24-byte thunk: calls Battle_Initialize and then falls through into the party status-flag refresh at 0x00607B94 (0x385D38-style split symbol). The long body Ghidra prints here belongs to that sibling.

The only code of its own is the Battle_Initialize call; the shared body tests vtable +0xE8 with ids 0x6A/0x6B/0x1A, i.e. battle status ids, so 'Visibility' was the wrong noun.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdatePartyStatusFlags

params.self: battle scene; +0x424 is the widget base

summary: For each party unit builds a three-bit mask from the unit's status tests (vtable +0x24 and +0xE8 with ids 0x6A/0x6B/0x1A) and refreshes widgets 1..3 whose bit changed.
evidence: The caller is the named Menu_UpdateSelectionWindow, so the BattleScene_ prefix was wrong, and the three ids passed to vtable +0xE8 are battle status ids (the same status-test shape FACTS.md records for 0x00639954), so the mask is status flags rather than visibility.

name: Menu_WindowLayout_Teardown

name: Field_NpcEntry_GetTalkAttrByte

name: maybe_Model_GetActorDisplayRecord

name: maybe_Menu_CloseWindowRestoreBgm

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_ApplyMemberDisplayByte
